scope.included: The full Video Agent v1 build as described by docs/HLD.md, decomposed against the ten canonical LLD modules and the PRD's delivery milestones, preceded by an M0 Foundation epic.
excluded: Everything in PRD §Out of scope (v1): dialogue and lip-sync, durations other than 40s, user-supplied reference characters, voiceover, an editing timeline, above 1080p.
The vector store, embed-default and realtime-voice — declared by the platform, unbuilt in v1 (D-13).
A human-review UI for ESCALATED (D-12): the data model and API expose it, no UI ships.
GitHub issue/milestone/label creation and any push — deliberately withheld; this plan is GitHub-ready only.

module_set.note: The ten canonical modules are fixed by the LLD set. Two scaffolding labels are used where work genuinely belongs to no canonical module: `foundation` (repo skeleton, toolchain, CI, dev stack) and `config` (settings and the alias/price tables). `config` already exists as a module key in .cdr/index/file.jsonl for .env.example.

settled_inputs: D-58 Magic Hour replaces Higgsfield MCP
D-59 no seed control; reproducibility promise partially unmet
D-60 cost in credits, reconciling ledger
D-01 2 repairs after the initial generation
D-39 0.75 is the QC accept gate
first_subtask_rationale: The repo is greenfield: no pyproject, no package, no tests. Every other subtask depends transitively on a package existing. S0.1.1 is the only subtask with zero dependencies that is not itself gated on an open question.

critical_path.description: Longest dependency chain through the plan. It runs foundation → persistence → gateway/harness → planning → graph → providers → Magic Hour adapter → frame chaining → QC → resume → observability → chaos. Every hop is a genuine prerequisite, not sequencing preference.

vertical_slice.name: Frame-chaining proof: plan story → lock bible → generate shot 1 → extract final frame → condition shot 2
vertical_slice.honest_assessment: Foundation genuinely gates this slice and it cannot be pulled earlier without faking it. Chaining requires: a package and settings; the persistence schema (shot_attempt carries request_fingerprint, without which a paid call can be double-billed the first time a worker dies); the gateway (the bible is an LLM product); the harness (nothing may call video.generate without a budget pre-flight); planning (there is no bible to chain against otherwise); the graph and checkpointer; the provider abstraction and the Magic Hour adapter; and ffmpeg frame extraction. That is the shortest real path.
what_is_legitimately_deferred: The QC gate — S2.3.3 runs with the accept-all qc_shot stub from S1.2.4, flagged in code and removed by S3.2.2. The slice proves chaining, not scoring.
The API job routes — the slice is driven from an integration test, not POST /v1/jobs.
Assembly stitch, deliver, the manifest, resume, and all of M5.
what_could_not_be_deferred: The shot_attempt request_fingerprint uniqueness and the in_flight write ordering. Deferring them would mean the first crash during the slice double-bills, and D-24 exists precisely to prevent that.
The harness budget pre-flight. A slice that can call a paid API with no cap is not a slice, it is an unbounded bill.

open_questions.question: What is `credits_per_usd`, and where is it configured?
open_questions.detail: providers.md §7.5 and D-60 require a CONFIGURED credits-to-USD rate, and ProviderProfile declares `credits_per_usd`. `.env.example` — which is the config contract — defines no such variable, and no LLD names one. Until it exists, BUDGET_MAX_USD_PER_JOB cannot be enforced against a provider that bills in credits, so the CPS hard USD cap is nominal. Also unspecified: `price_per_second` per provider, needed for the pre-flight estimate.
open_questions.why_not_guessed: Guessing a rate would make the one non-negotiable budget control silently wrong in whichever direction the guess erred. pending.md already records this as needing a real number.
open_questions.proposed_resolution: Add MAGICHOUR_CREDITS_PER_USD and MAGICHOUR_PRICE_PER_SECOND_CREDITS to .env.example (a documentation-run amendment), sourced from real Magic Hour pricing.

open_questions.question: Who produces the >=200-pair QC labelled calibration set, and what funds the clips?
open_questions.detail: qc.md §5 makes calibration a first-class deliverable with enforced targets (D-40) and a CI gate. The set does not exist. Building it needs ~200 real generated shot pairs — i.e. real Magic Hour credit spend — plus per-dimension human labelling. pending.md flags it as an M4 delivery dependency but assigns no owner, no budget and no labelling protocol.
open_questions.why_not_guessed: A synthetic or self-labelled set would calibrate QC against itself and the false-pass target would be meaningless. This is a data-acquisition project, not a coding task.
open_questions.proposed_resolution: Scope it as its own work item with a credit budget and a labelling rubric before M4 starts; S3.1.8 ships the harness and the gate against a placeholder set and turns the gate on when the real set lands.

open_questions.question: What is the job queue / worker transport?
open_questions.detail: api.md says POST /v1/jobs 'enqueues' and never does work inline; graph.md and harness.md assume a worker process; persistence.md §5 lists Redis uses and includes no queue. No LLD names a transport (Redis stream, arq, Celery, a Postgres-backed queue) and `.env.example` has no queue variable. An implementer must invent one.
open_questions.why_not_guessed: The choice determines at-least-once vs at-most-once semantics, which interacts directly with the anti-double-bill guarantees in D-24 and the one-writer-per-job lock in D-10. It is an architecture decision, not an implementation detail.
open_questions.proposed_resolution: An architecture decision recording the transport and its delivery semantics, then an amendment to graph.md or a new LLD section, before S1.4.1.

open_questions.question: What authentication scheme resolves a request to a Principal?
open_questions.detail: api.md §6 requires every request to resolve to Principal {tenant_id, subject, scopes} and makes it the sole source of the RLS tenant setting — the single most load-bearing security boundary in the system. No LLD names the scheme (JWT? issuer? API key? rotation?) and `.env.example` has no auth variable.
open_questions.why_not_guessed: Inventing a token format in a subtask would bake an unreviewed security decision into the RLS boundary.
open_questions.proposed_resolution: Decide the scheme and add its variables to `.env.example`. S0.4.2 ships the Principal boundary and a pluggable verifier so the rest of the API is unblocked; the verifier implementation lands with the decision.

open_questions.question: What is the licensed local music library, and how does a plan's tone select a track?
open_questions.detail: assembly.md §4.3 requires tracks from a licensed local library 'selected by the plan's tone', never generated and never fetched from the open internet. No library exists, no path is configured, and no tone-to-track mapping is defined.
open_questions.why_not_guessed: The music bed is optional and off by default (D-48), and its failure is explicitly non-fatal, so this does not block the critical path. But shipping a selection rule invented in a subtask would be a product decision made by an implementer.
open_questions.proposed_resolution: Ship the mechanism, the fade/loudness/trim behaviour and the non-fatal failure path in S2.4.5 against an empty library (every job delivers silent, flagged). Populate the library and the selection rule as a separate product item.

open_questions.question: Is there a `tenant` table, and what does `tenant_id` reference?
open_questions.detail: persistence.md §2 puts `tenant_id UUID NOT NULL` on every table and D-51 denormalises it so RLS is never a join — but the DDL never defines a `tenant` table. `job.tenant_id` therefore references nothing. RLS works regardless (the predicate is a session setting), but tenant provisioning, per-tenant budget config (`max_usd` is described as 'per-tenant config') and per-tenant retention policy all have nowhere to live.
open_questions.why_not_guessed: Adding a table to the canonical schema is a documentation change, not an implementation choice, and it must go through the CDR drift gate.
open_questions.proposed_resolution: Amend persistence.md §2 with a `tenant` table carrying at least id, budget config and retention policy, then land S0.5.2 against the amended DDL.

open_questions.question: Is the 0.75 continuity threshold a compile-time constant or configuration?
open_questions.detail: qc.md §2 declares `CONTINUITY_THRESHOLD: Final[float] = 0.75` and §5 says explicitly that 'the threshold stays 0.75 because it is a product commitment, not a tunable'; §9 requires the constant to appear in exactly one place. `.env.example` nonetheless exposes `QC_ACCEPT_THRESHOLD=0.75` and `QC_MAX_REPAIR_ATTEMPTS=2`. The two documents contradict each other, and the brief says the `.env.example` names are contract.
open_questions.why_not_guessed: Either reading is defensible and they produce different code. Making it configurable weakens a stated product commitment; ignoring the env var breaks the config contract. Reconciling them silently would hide a real conflict between two canonical documents.
open_questions.proposed_resolution: Most likely resolution: keep both env vars as startup-validated values that must equal 0.75 and 2 in v1, so the config contract holds and the commitment is enforced at boot. This needs a product ruling, not an implementer's choice.

open_questions.question: Who authors the four registry prompts, and how is a fresh environment bootstrapped?
open_questions.detail: observability.md §3 makes the Langfuse prompt registry the only prompt source and makes a raw prompt string in code a CI failure. The four prompts — story_plan, continuity_bible, qc_continuity, repair_delta — do not exist. No LLD assigns authorship or describes bootstrapping an empty Langfuse project, so a fresh checkout cannot run a single node.
open_questions.why_not_guessed: The mechanism is unambiguous and is planned (seeding scripts in S1.1.6 and S3.1.7); only the prompt content and its ownership are unassigned, which does not block the surrounding code.
open_questions.proposed_resolution: Ship the idempotent seeding scripts with first-pass prompt text authored alongside; treat prompt quality as an eval-driven iteration, not a blocker.

open_questions.question: Does a FAILED job that still delivered plan and bible JSON count toward the '< 1% zero deliverable' metric?
open_questions.detail: HLD §11 defines the metric as terminal jobs with outcome FAILED/FAILED_NO_PROGRESS AND zero delivered artifacts. But assembly.md §5 says the zero-usable-clip case (VA-ASM-002) still returns the plan and bible JSON — which are artifacts. Read literally, the PRD's headline failure case can never be counted, and the metric always reads 0%.
open_questions.why_not_guessed: It changes what a headline success metric measures.
open_questions.proposed_resolution: Define 'zero deliverable' as zero *media* artifacts (no MP4 and no clips), and say so in observability.md §7. S4.2.1 must implement whichever definition is ruled.

open_questions.question: Is `CreateJobRequest.webhook_url` a real feature?
open_questions.detail: api.md §2.2 declares `webhook_url: HttpUrl | None` on the create request, but no LLD describes a client-callback delivery: no payload shape, no retry policy, no signing, no failure behaviour, and no mention in the progress or delivery sections. It is either a dead field or a missing feature.
open_questions.why_not_guessed: Implementing an unspecified outbound webhook would invent a public contract.
open_questions.proposed_resolution: Either remove the field from api.md or specify the callback. No subtask implements it as planned; SSE (S1.3.5) is the only progress channel in scope.

github.title: [M0] Foundation
github.body:
The skeleton every later milestone assumes but the PRD never names: Python 3.12 project, FastAPI async shell, toolchain, settings bound to the .env.example contract, the Postgres schema with RLS and expand/contract migrations, the LiteLLM gateway with its alias table and retry/fallback/circuit-break policy, and the harness loop engine with its budget caps.

Scope note: the error-code enum, JSON logging and the redaction serialiser are pulled forward from M5 into M0 because every module below raises stable codes and logs; the Langfuse trace model, scores, metrics and CI gates stay in M5.

epics.title: Job lifecycle, planning and the continuity bible

github.title: [M1-M2] Job lifecycle, planning and the continuity bible
github.body: The job lifecycle end to end up to the point where pixels would be generated: the API surface with idempotency, the compiled StateGraph with checkpointing, the worker runtime, and the two planning nodes whose outputs every later stage depends on. At the end of this epic a job can be created, planned, have its bible locked, and terminate cleanly with stub generation.

epics.title: Video provider, frame chaining and assembly

github.title: [M3] Video provider, frame chaining and assembly
github.body:
The product's entire value proposition. Magic Hour replaces the PRD's Higgsfield MCP (D-58); the abstraction absorbs the swap and the word `magichour` appears in exactly one adapter module and in config. The vertical slice that proves frame chaining — plan story, lock bible, generate shot 1, extract its final frame, condition shot 2 on that frame — becomes reachable inside this epic at S2.3.3.

No test in this epic may call the live Magic Hour API. All upstream behaviour is exercised through fake providers and recorded HTTP transcripts.

epics.title: QC loop, partial results and resume

github.title: [M4] QC loop, partial results and resume
github.body: The detective and corrective half of the continuity thesis, plus the two resilience affordances the PRD promises. This epic closes the repair back-edge — the only cycle in the graph — and removes the unconditional-accept QC stub introduced for the M3 vertical slice.

epics.title: Observability, cost caps, load and chaos

github.title: [M5] Observability, cost caps, load and chaos
github.body: The Langfuse trace model, the metric bindings that make the PRD's targets measurable, the CI gates, and the load and chaos testing that proves the four termination outcomes hold under real failure. The error taxonomy, logging and redaction substrate already landed in M0.

github.title: [T0.1] Repo skeleton and toolchain
github.body: Greenfield repo. Nothing exists: no pyproject, no package, no tests, no CI.

github.title: [T0.2] Configuration contract and alias table
github.body: `.env.example` is the contract. Variable names are fixed; subtasks consume them rather than inventing new ones. The alias table is the only place a model name may exist.

github.title: [T0.3] Error taxonomy and logging substrate
github.body: Pulled forward from M5. Every module below raises a stable code and logs a JSON line; neither is possible without this. Langfuse tracing itself stays in M5.

github.title: [T0.4] FastAPI application shell
github.body: The async surface with nothing on it yet: app factory, health, auth dependency, tenant-scoped DB session, error envelope. Job routes arrive in M1-M2.

tasks.title: PostgreSQL schema, RLS and expand/contract migrations

github.title: [T0.5] PostgreSQL schema, RLS and expand/contract migrations
github.body: Postgres is the system of record. RLS on every table without exception, and migrations that are expand/contract and applied before deploy. The DDL in persistence.md §2 is the public interface.

github.title: [T0.6] Redis and artifact storage
github.body: Redis holds cache, locks, rate limits, idempotency and progress and is never authoritative. The object store holds bytes; Postgres holds only metadata and keys.

tasks.title: LiteLLM gateway: alias resolution and failure policy

github.title: [T0.7] LiteLLM gateway: alias resolution and failure policy
github.body: The only path from application code to an LLM. Video generation does not traverse it (D-06) but shares its policy engine, so the two egresses cannot drift.

tasks.title: Harness loop engine, budgets and termination

github.title: [T0.8] Harness loop engine, budgets and termination
github.body: The harness owns context, tools, budgets and termination. `decide()` is the only function in the system that may end a job. It must not import any domain module.

github.title: [T1.1] Planning module: StoryPlan and ContinuityBible
github.body: Both artifacts are delivered to the user as machine-readable JSON and are therefore a public contract, not internal scratch. A schema change here is a breaking API change.

tasks.title: Graph topology, checkpointing and the harness veto

github.title: [T1.2] Graph topology, checkpointing and the harness veto
github.body: The compiled StateGraph owns topology and state. It contains no domain logic: each node is a thin adapter. It does not decide whether to stop.

github.title: [T1.3] API job lifecycle routes
github.body: Accepts a prompt and creates a Job, never doing the work inline. Idempotency on every work-creating POST, with no exceptions and no 'optional in dev'.

github.title: [T1.4] Worker runtime
github.body: The process that actually runs graphs. No LLD names the queue transport — see OPEN_QUESTION Q3.

tasks.title: Provider abstraction: protocol, negotiation, failover, composition

github.title: [T2.1] Provider abstraction: protocol, negotiation, failover, composition
github.body: Magic Hour is the first adapter, not the interface. Nothing in this task may name a provider.

github.title: [T2.2] Magic Hour adapter
github.body: The one module in the tree where the string `magichour` may appear. Only the facts in `providers.md` §7 are contractual; nothing outside that section may be assumed about the upstream API. No test may hit the live API.

tasks.title: Frame extraction and the chaining vertical slice

github.title: [T2.3] Frame extraction and the chaining vertical slice
github.body: The producer side of the chaining contract plus the two node bodies that close the loop. S2.3.3 is the point at which the frame-chaining vertical slice becomes runnable end to end.

github.title: [T2.4] Assembly, delivery and the manifest
github.body: All media manipulation. Nothing else in the system shells out to ffmpeg.

github.title: [T3.1] QC scoring
github.body: Scores a clip against the locked bible per dimension with rationale. It does not decide the next node: it emits a score, and the graph compares it to a threshold this module owns, under the harness veto.

tasks.title: The repair loop and the back-edge

github.title: [T3.2] The repair loop and the back-edge
github.body: The only cycle in the graph, bounded three ways: the repair cap, the shot-scope failure signature, and the harness's max_iterations. Any one of them alone terminates the loop.

github.title: [T3.3] Partial results
github.body: The mechanism behind 'never returns nothing'. Only the zero-usable-shot case produces no deliverable, and that is the case the PRD budgets at < 1%.

github.title: [T3.4] Resume and shot-level regeneration
github.body: Resume, don't restart. Completed shots are never regenerated or re-billed — a promise this strong gets two independent guards and an assertion, not just a checkpoint restore.

tasks.title: Langfuse trace, span, generation and score model

github.title: [T4.1] Langfuse trace, span, generation and score model
github.body: Trace = one unit of work. Spans = graph nodes. Generations = LLM calls. A repair is visible as structure — a second generate_shot span — not as a log message.

github.title: [T4.2] Metric instrumentation and CI gates
github.body: Unmeasurable targets are not targets. Each PRD success metric is bound to a concrete measurement, and CI gates on eval regression > 3% and cost regression > 20%.

github.title: [T4.3] Cost cap hardening
github.body: Cross-module verification that the USD cap is real, now that credits, reconciliation and refunds all exist.

github.title: [T4.4] Load and chaos
github.body: Prove the four termination outcomes hold under real failure, and that the p90 latency target is measurable.

subtasks.title: Python 3.12 project skeleton and pyproject

github.title: [S0.1.1] Python 3.12 project skeleton and pyproject
github.body: Create `pyproject.toml` (PEP 621, Python 3.12, uv or pip-tools lock), the `src/video_agent/` package with one empty sub-package per module in the fixed ten-module set plus `config/`, and `src/video_agent/__init__.py` exposing `__version__`. Runtime deps pinned: fastapi, uvicorn, pydantic v2, pydantic-settings, sqlalchemy[asyncio], asyncpg, alembic, redis, httpx, langgraph, langfuse, boto3.

acceptance_criteria: `pip install -e .` succeeds on Python 3.12 and fails on 3.11 (`requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.13"`).
`import video_agent` succeeds and `video_agent.__version__` is a non-empty string.
The package contains exactly these sub-packages: api, harness, gateway, graph, planning, providers, qc, assembly, persistence, observability, config.
A lock file is committed and `--frozen`/`--require-hashes` install reproduces it byte-for-byte.
No module contains anything but `__init__.py` — this commit adds no behaviour.
test_spec: test_package_imports — `import video_agent` and each of the eleven sub-packages import cleanly.

test_module_set_is_exactly_ten_plus_config — enumerate `video_agent.__path__` sub-packages and assert set equality against the fixed list; guards against a twelfth module appearing without a doc change.
test_python_version_floor — assert `sys.version_info[:2] == (3, 12)` in CI.
traceability: state.md: module set is fixed at the ten LLDs

subtasks.title: Lint, format and strict type-check toolchain

github.title: [S0.1.2] Lint, format and strict type-check toolchain
github.body: Configure ruff (lint + format) and mypy in strict mode over `src/`, add pre-commit hooks and a `Makefile` with `make lint`, `make type`, `make test`, `make check`. Zero baseline suppressions: an empty package must pass clean.

acceptance_criteria: `make lint` exits 0 with zero findings on the current tree.
`make type` runs mypy with `strict = true`, `disallow_any_generics`, `warn_unused_ignores`, and exits 0.
`# type: ignore` without a specific error code is a lint error.
`pre-commit run --all-files` exits 0.
Neither tool is configured with a per-file ignore list at this commit.
test_spec: test_lint_config_has_no_blanket_ignores — parse `pyproject.toml`, assert `tool.ruff.lint.ignore` and `tool.mypy.overrides` are empty.
test_mypy_strict_enabled — assert `tool.mypy.strict is True`.
test_make_check_runs_all_three — invoke `make check --dry-run` and assert lint, type and test targets are all reached.

subtasks.title: pytest harness and CI workflow

github.title: [S0.1.3] pytest harness and CI workflow
github.body: Add pytest + pytest-asyncio (strict mode) + coverage, the `tests/{unit,integration,contract}` layout, shared async fixtures, and a CI workflow running lint, type and unit tests on every push. Integration tests are collected but skipped when the dev stack is absent.

acceptance_criteria: `make test` runs and reports coverage; the run is green with zero tests collected being an error (`--strict-markers`, and a placeholder test exists).
`asyncio_mode = strict` is set — an `async def` test without a marker fails collection rather than being silently skipped.
CI fails the build if lint, type or unit tests fail.
Integration tests marked `@pytest.mark.integration` are deselected by default and selected by `make test-integration`.
Coverage is reported but not yet gated (no threshold at this commit).
test_spec: test_asyncio_strict_mode — assert `asyncio_mode` is `strict` in config.
test_integration_marker_deselected_by_default — run pytest collection with default args against a fixture module containing one integration-marked test; assert it is deselected.
test_ci_workflow_gates_three_jobs — parse the CI workflow YAML; assert lint, type and test steps exist and none is `continue-on-error`.

subtasks.title: Dev stack compose file and ffmpeg version assertion

github.title: [S0.1.4] Dev stack compose file and ffmpeg version assertion
github.body: `docker-compose.dev.yml` bringing up PostgreSQL 16, Redis 7, an S3-compatible object store and the LiteLLM proxy, wired to the `.env.example` variable names. Add a startup assertion that the ffmpeg and ffprobe binaries are present and at the pinned version.

acceptance_criteria: `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d` yields four healthy containers.
Every service's connection string in the compose file matches the default value of its `.env.example` variable (DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, ARTIFACT_ENDPOINT_URL, LITELLM_BASE_URL).
`assert_media_toolchain()` raises `RuntimeError` naming the expected and actual version when ffmpeg differs from the pin, and returns None when it matches.
The application refuses to start (non-zero exit, no port bound) when the ffmpeg version assertion fails.
No credential values appear in the compose file; only variable references.
test_spec: test_compose_urls_match_env_example — parse both files; assert each service URL equals the corresponding `.env.example` default.
test_ffmpeg_version_mismatch_refuses_start — monkeypatch the version probe to return a wrong version; assert `assert_media_toolchain()` raises and the message contains both expected and actual.
test_ffmpeg_missing_binary_refuses_start — monkeypatch the probe to raise FileNotFoundError; assert a clear error, not a traceback leak.
test_compose_contains_no_literal_secrets — grep the compose file for `mhk_live_`, `sk-`, and any non-empty value for a `*_KEY` variable.
traceability: assembly.md §7 (ffmpeg version pinned and asserted at startup)
assembly.md §8 (ffmpeg version drift → refuse to start)

subtasks.title: Typed settings bound to the .env.example contract

github.title: [S0.2.1] Typed settings bound to the .env.example contract
github.body: A `pydantic-settings` `Settings` object with exactly one field per variable in `.env.example`, using the same names. Fail-fast at import: a missing required variable raises before any port is bound. Secrets are `SecretStr` so they cannot be accidentally stringified.

acceptance_criteria: Every variable name in `.env.example` has a corresponding `Settings` field with the identical name (case-insensitive env binding).
`Settings()` with an empty environment raises `ValidationError` naming every missing required variable in one message, not the first one only.
`MAGICHOUR_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `MAGICHOUR_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and the three upstream LLM keys are typed `SecretStr`.
`repr(settings)` and `settings.model_dump_json()` render every SecretStr as `**********` and never the value.
`MAGICHOUR_RESOLUTION` is constrained to `Literal["720p","1080p"]`; `QC_ACCEPT_THRESHOLD` to `[0,1]`; `QC_MAX_REPAIR_ATTEMPTS` to exactly 2 (see OPEN_QUESTION Q7 before relaxing).
No new environment variable is introduced by this commit.
test_spec: test_settings_fields_match_env_example_exactly — parse `.env.example`, diff its key set against `Settings.model_fields`; assert both directions are empty. This is the contract test.
test_missing_required_reports_all — empty env; assert the ValidationError body names DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL and MAGICHOUR_API_KEY together.
test_secrets_never_stringify — assert `str(settings)`, `repr(settings)` and `model_dump_json()` contain none of the planted secret values.
test_resolution_literal_rejects_4k — `MAGICHOUR_RESOLUTION=4k` raises (1080p is a hard ceiling).
test_repair_cap_rejects_three — `QC_MAX_REPAIR_ATTEMPTS=3` raises; the DB CHECK is the last line of defence but config is the first.

subtasks.title: Alias table and model price table loader

github.title: [S0.2.2] Alias table and model price table loader
github.body: `config/aliases.yaml` — the only file in the tree where a concrete model name may appear — with primary/fallbacks/canary and `required_capabilities` per alias, plus a per-model price table. A typed loader validates it at startup and fails closed on an unknown alias.

acceptance_criteria: The loader parses `config/aliases.yaml` into typed objects and raises `VA-GW-002` at startup when any of the five aliases in the `Alias` enum is absent.
Every alias entry validates: exactly one primary, zero or more fallbacks, at most one canary with `traffic_pct` in 0..100.
A model referenced by any alias but missing from the price table fails startup validation with a config alarm — it is never priced at zero.
`realtime-voice` and `embed-default` may be declared with no consumer and must not fail validation (D-13).
The loaded table is immutable at runtime; there is no setter.
test_spec: test_missing_alias_fails_closed — remove `vision-default` from a fixture YAML; assert startup raises VA-GW-002.
test_unpriced_model_fails_startup — a fallback model absent from the price table; assert startup raises rather than defaulting to 0.
test_canary_pct_bounds — 101 and -1 are rejected.
test_unconsumed_aliases_allowed — a YAML declaring realtime-voice and embed-default with no consumer validates.
test_price_table_golden — golden snapshot of parsed prices; a silent price edit fails CI.

subtasks.title: CI static guards for the alias-only and no-inline-prompt rules

github.title: [S0.2.3] CI static guards for the alias-only and no-inline-prompt rules
github.body: Three CI checks, each a test so they run locally too: (1) no vendor or provider name — `magichour`, `higgsfield`, every member of the Magic Hour model enum, and every LLM vendor name — appears outside the Magic Hour adapter module and `config/`; (2) no raw prompt string literal in application code; (3) no comparison of `model_used` or `provider_key` against a literal.

acceptance_criteria: The provider-name grep passes on the current tree and fails when a test fixture plants `magichour` in `src/video_agent/graph/`.

subtasks.title: POST /v1/jobs with the full idempotency algorithm

github.title: [S1.3.1] POST /v1/jobs with the full idempotency algorithm
github.body: `202 Accepted`, never `200`. The idempotency algorithm executed inside a Redis lock keyed on `(tenant_id, route, key)`: fingerprint the canonical body, `SET NX EX 86400`, replay on a fingerprint match, `409` on a mismatch, `409 + Retry-After` while in flight. The same key with a different body yields `409 VA-REQ-003` and creates no second job.
A concurrent duplicate while the first is in flight yields `409 VA-REQ-004` with `Retry-After`.
Redis unavailable yields `503` and no job — idempotency is a non-negotiable and may not be degraded like a cache (D-17).
The create path does O(1) work: one Redis round trip and two inserts, with no provider or model call reachable from it.
